grammarPoints.title: **I am going to visit Singapore tomorrow.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription:
未み来らいを　表あらわす：**be going to**＋動どう詞しの原げん形けい「…するつもりです」など　あらかじめ
決きめておいた　予よ定ていや　未み来らいの　ことを　表あらわすには、 〈am [are, is] going to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉を　使つかう。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This structure, using be going to followed by the base form of the verb, expresses a future action that has already been planned or decided upon beforehand (a set intention or future event). It translates to 'I intend to...' or 'I am going to....'
examples: **Are you going to visit Singapore tomorrow?**
**I will make a reservation.**

grammarPoints.title: **I will make a reservation.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription:
助じょ動どう詞し：**will**「これから　…しよう」と　そのときに　決きめた　予よ定ていや
未み来らいの　ことを　表あらわすには　〈will ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉を　使つかう。 また、「…でしょう」「…するつもりです」など　未み来らいの
予よ測そくや　意い志しを　表あらわす　ときにも　使つかう。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Use the structure 〈will + base form of the verb〉 to express a decision or plan made at the moment of speaking, referring to the immediate future, translated as 'I will do....'. It is also used to express future prediction or willingness ('...will probably...' or 'I intend to...').
examples: **You will see the sea very soon.**
**You’ll see the Merlion soon.**

grammarPoints.title: **I will show you some pictures.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription:
文法ぶんぽう用よう語ご（文ぶん構こう造ぞう）：SVOO（第だい4文ぶん型けい）show, make, buy, teach, giveなど ＋ （人ひと） ＋ （もの）
「（人ひと）に　（もの）を　…する」という　意い味みに　なる。動どう詞しの
あとが、「だれ（人ひと）に ＋ 何なに（もの）を」の　順じゅん
になっていることに　注ちゅう意いする。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This structure (Subject + Verb + Indirect Object (person) + Direct Object (thing)) means 'to do (the action) of the verb to (a person) with (a thing)'. Pay attention that the word order after the verb is always 'who (person) to whom/what (thing)'.
examples: I’ll **show you a video**.
I will **tell** my aunt **some interesting things about Singapore**.

grammarPoints.title: **People call this area Little India.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 文法ぶんぽう用よう語ご（文ぶん構こう造ぞう）：SVOC（第だい5文ぶん型けい）2 には、動どう詞し（call）の　あとに　2つの　かたまりが　あり、our dog ＝ Pochiの　関かん係けいです。 このような　場ば合あい、our dogを　目もく的てき語ご、Pochiのほうは　補ほ語ごと　いいます。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: In this structure (Subject + Verb + Object + Complement), the verb (like 'call') is followed by two elements where the Object and the Complement are related (e.g., 'our dog' equals 'Pochi'). The second element (Complement) explains the state or condition of the Object.
examples: We **call our dog Pochi**.
We **call our dog Pochi**.

grammarPoints.title: **When I go to a ramen restaurant, I order tonkotsu ramen.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription:
接せつ続ぞく詞し：**when**when ...は、「…（の）
ときに」という　意い味みに なる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The subordinating conjunction 'when' is used to connect two clauses and means 'at the time when...'. The 'when' clause can appear at the start or end of the sentence. If placed first, use a comma before the main clause.
examples: **When I eat breakfast, I watch the news on TV.**
**I order tonkotsu ramen when I go to a ramen restaurant.**

grammarPoints.title: **If you have time, you can come.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 接せつ続ぞく詞し：**if**「（もし）…ならば」と　条じょう件けんを　表あらわすには、ifを　使つかう。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The conjunction 'if' is used to express a condition, meaning '(If)... then...'. Note that even when referring to a future condition, the verb following 'if' must be in the present tense.
examples: **If you love ramen, I’ll tell you about some good restaurants.**
**You can come if you have time.**

grammarPoints.title: **I like Sapporo ramen because the soup is thick.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 接せつ続ぞく詞し：**because**「（なぜなら）…だから」と 理り由ゆうを　表あらわすには、becauseを　使つかう。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The conjunction 'because' is used to state a reason, meaning '(because)... therefore'. The 'because' clause can appear at the start or end of the sentence. If placed first, use a comma before the main clause.
examples: **I enjoy Japanese sweets because they look beautiful.**
**Because the soup is thick, I like Sapporo ramen.**

grammarPoints.title: **I think (that) food travels around the world.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription:
接せつ続ぞく詞し：**that**think (that) ...は、「…と　思おもう」という　意い味みに　なる。thatは　省しょう略りゃくされる　ことが　多おお
い。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The structure 'think (that)...' means 'I believe that...' or 'I am of the opinion that...'. The word 'that' introduces a noun clause that acts as the object of the verb 'think', and it is often omitted in casual speech or writing.
examples: **Eddy thinks (that) food culture is always changing.**
**I think chefs use local ingredients in ramen.**

grammarPoints.title: **I use a computer to study English.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription:
不ふ定てい詞し（副ふく詞してき用よう法ほう）：「…する　ために」という　意い味みを
表あらわすには、 〈to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉を　使つかう。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: Use the infinitive phrase 〈to + base form of the verb〉 to express purpose, meaning 'in order to...' or 'to do...'. This phrase functions adverbially, modifying the main verb.
examples: **I went to a bookstore to look for interesting comic books.**
**I got up early to see the new movie.**

grammarPoints.title: **I am happy to hear that.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription:
不ふ定てい詞し（原げん因いんを　表あらわす　副ふく詞してき用よう法ほう）：〈to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉が、「…して」（感かん情じょうの　原げん因いんを　表あらわす）の　意い味みに
なる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The infinitive phrase 〈to + base form of the verb〉 can follow adjectives expressing emotion (like happy, surprised, sad) to indicate the cause or reason for that emotion, meaning 'I am (emotion) because of/to....'
examples: **I’m excited to go to a car factory.**
**I was glad to see their happy faces.**

grammarPoints.title: **She has a lot of work to do.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription:
不ふ定てい詞し（形けい容よう詞してき用よう法ほう）：〈to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉が　すぐ前まえの　（代だい）名めい詞しを　修しゅう飾しょくして　説せつ明めいを　加くわえ、「…すべき」
「…する　ための」という　意い味みに　なる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The infinitive phrase 〈to + base form of the verb〉 modifies the preceding (pro)noun, functioning adjectivally. It means 'work to be done' or 'things needed to...'
examples: **I have various things to study.**
**Asakusa is the place to visit.**

grammarPoints.title: **It is important to look at the children’s faces.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 不ふ定てい詞し（名めい詞してき用よう法ほう）：It is ... ＋ to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい「～するのは　…です」という　意い味みに　なる。この　itは、to以い下の　内ない容ようを　示しめす。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This structure uses the indefinite pronoun 'It' as a temporary subject, and the infinitive phrase (to + base form of the verb) provides the real subject, meaning 'To do (action) is (adjective)'. This is used to state that performing an action is necessary or noteworthy.
examples: **It is necessary to watch the children carefully.**
**It is interesting to learn English.**

grammarPoints.title: **You have to speak English. You do not have to speak perfect English.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 文法ぶんぽう用よう語ご（助じょ動どう詞し）：**have to**＋動どう詞しの原げん形けい「…しなければならない」と　必ひつ要よう性せいや　義ぎ務むを表あらわすには、〈have to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉を　使つかう。否ひ定てい文ぶんでは、「…しなくて　よい」という　意い味みになる。主しゅ語ごが　三人にん称しょう　単たん数すうの　ときは、has to、does not have toと　なる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The structure 〈have to + base form of the verb〉 expresses necessity or obligation, meaning 'must' or 'need to'. In the negative form, 'do not have to' (or 'does not have to' for third person singular), it means 'it is not necessary to...', or 'do not need to...'
examples: **We have to bring our lunch.**
**I don’t have to take a map.**

grammarPoints.title: **We must save water. We must not take long showers.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription:
助じょ動どう詞し：**must**「…しなければならない」と　義ぎ務むや　命めい令れいを
表あらわすには、〈must ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉を　使つかう。 否ひ定てい文ぶんでは、「…してはならない」と　禁きん止しを
表あらわす。短たん縮しゅく形けいは　mustn’tと　なる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The structure 〈must + base form of the verb〉 expresses strong obligation or command, meaning 'it is absolutely necessary to...'. In the negative form, 'must not' (or 'mustn’t'), it expresses prohibition, meaning 'must not do...'
examples: **You must stay with us.**
**You must not make a fire.**

grammarPoints.title: **They enjoy reading books.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 動どう名めい詞し：動どう詞しに　ingが　ついた　形かたちは、進しん行こう形けいで　使つかう　ほかにも、「…すること」という　名めい詞しの　働はたらきを　する。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The -ing form added to a verb (gerund) functions as a noun, meaning 'the act of doing...'. It is used here as the object of a verb like 'enjoy'.
examples: **They finished eating lunch.**
**I enjoy swimming in the sea.**

grammarPoints.title: **Talking with him was fun.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription:
動どう名めい詞し：動どう詞しに　ingが　ついた　形かたち（「…すること」）を　主しゅ語ごとして　使つかう
ことも　できる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The -ing form added to a verb (gerund) can function as the subject of a sentence, meaning 'The act of doing...' is/was (adjective). When used as a subject, it takes the singular form of the verb (is/was).
examples: **Walking together was nice.**
**Taking pictures of animals is interesting.**

grammarPoints.title: **I know how to use these products.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し ＋ to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい：howや　whatの　あとに　〈to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉が　続つづくと、「どのように　…するか」「何なにを　…すべきか」という　意い味みに　なる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The structure of an interrogative word (like how, what, where) followed by 〈to + base form of the verb〉 functions nominally, meaning 'how to do...', 'what to do...', or 'where to find...'. This phrase usually acts as the object of the main verb.
examples: **Anna knows when to leave her house.**
**I can tell you where to find facilities with a universal design in our city, if you want.**

grammarPoints.title: **I can show you how to use these products.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 主しゅ語ご ＋ 動どう詞し ＋（人ひと）＋ 疑ぎ問もん詞し ＋ to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい：「（人ひと）に（どのように　…するか）を　～する」と いう　意い味みに　なる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: This structure involves a verb that takes both an indirect object (person) and a complex object (interrogative + infinitive phrase). It means 'I can show (a person) how to do (an action)' or 'I can tell (a person) where to find (something)'.
examples: **I can tell you how to use these scissors.**
**I will show you where to find accessible restrooms.**

grammarPoints.title: **I am sure that these ideas help many people.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 主しゅ語ご ＋ be動どう詞し ＋ 形けい容よう詞し ＋ that感かん情じょうや　心しん理り　を表あらわす　形けい容よう詞しの　あとに　that ...を 続つづけると、「きっと　…だ」「…して　うれしい」などという　意い味みに　なる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: When an adjective expressing feeling or mental state (like sure, glad) is followed by a 'that' clause, it means 'I am certain that...' or 'I am happy that...'. This structure clearly states the speaker's conviction or emotion regarding the following clause.
examples: **I think the ramp is great.**
**I am glad that you became interested in universal design.**

grammarPoints.title: **A volleyball is smaller than a basketball. A volleyball is the smallest of the three.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription:
比較ひかく級きゅう、最さい上じょう級きゅう：２つの　ものを　比くらべて　「～よりも…」と　言いう　ときは　比較ひかく級きゅう（...er）を　使つかう。３つ以い上じょうの　ものを　比くらべて　「いちばん…」と　言いう
ときは　〈the ＋ 最さい上じょう級きゅう（...est）〉を　使つかう。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: To compare two items, use the comparative form (-er, followed by 'than') meaning 'more/less than...'. To compare three or more items, use the superlative form (the -est), meaning 'the most/least... of all'.
examples: **A basketball is bigger than a tennis ball.**
**A tennis ball is the smallest of the five.**

grammarPoints.title: **This sport is more interesting than that one. This sport is the most interesting sport of all.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription:
比較ひかく級きゅう、最さい上じょう級きゅう：比較ひかく的てきつづりの　長ながい　形けい容よう詞しや
副ふく詞しの　場ば合あい、比較ひかく級きゅうは　more ...、
最さい上じょう級きゅうは　most ...と　なる。
最さい上じょう級きゅうには　theを　つける。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: For adjectives or adverbs with longer spellings (typically three or more syllables), the comparative form uses 'more...' (followed by 'than'), and the superlative form uses 'the most...'. Remember to use 'the' with the superlative form.
examples: **This sport is more exciting than that one.**
**Soccer is the most exciting sport of all.**

grammarPoints.title: **Many of our classmates like other sports better than basketball. Seven of them like tennis the best.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: betterと best：goodや　well、very muchの　場ば合あい、比較ひかく級きゅうは　better、 最さい上じょう級きゅうは　bestと　なる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The irregular comparative form of 'good' (adjective), 'well' (adverb), and 'like... very much' (idiom) is 'better', and the superlative form is 'best'. These irregular forms do not follow the standard -er/-est or more/most patterns.
examples: **I like English the best of all subjects.**
**I like pizza better than sushi.**

grammarPoints.title: **Soccer is as popular as tennis.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription:
as ＋ 原げん級きゅう ＋ as：as ... as ～は　「～と　同おなじくらい…」、not as ... as ～では
「～ほど…ではない」という　意い味みに　なる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The phrase 'as ... as ~' is used to show that two things are equal in degree regarding the adjective or adverb used, meaning 'the same degree of... as...'. The phrase 'not as ... as ~' means 'not to the same degree as...'
examples: **Your presentation was as good as Riko’s.**
**Pandas are as cute as rabbits.**

grammarPoints.title: **This place is selected as a World Heritage site.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 受うけ身み：「…されます」、「…されています」と　言いう　ときは、〈be動どう詞し＋ 過か去こ分ぶん詞し〉で 表あらわす。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: The passive voice uses the structure 〈be verb + past participle〉 to express an action done to the subject ('...is/are done', '...has been done'). It shifts the focus to the receiver of the action rather than the actor.
examples: **Was this shirt made in South Africa?**
**It is called the Cape Floral Region.**

grammarPoints.title: **Is it called the Cape Floral Region? ―Yes, it is. [No, it is not.]**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 受うけ身みの　疑ぎ問もん文ぶん：受うけ身みの　疑ぎ問もん文ぶんでは、be動どう詞しを　主しゅ語ごの　前まえに　置おく。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: To form a question in the passive voice, place the appropriate 'be' verb (is, are, was, were) before the subject. The main verb remains in the past participle form.
examples: **Is it called the Cape Floral Region?**
**Is this stadium used for rugby matches?**

grammarPoints.title: **The Taj Mahal is loved by many people.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: byつきの　受うけ身み：受うけ身みに　by ...が　つくと、「…によって」という　意い味みに　なる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: When the passive voice includes the phrase 'by...', it identifies the agent—the person or thing performing the action. This translates to '...is done by...'. This is used when the actor is important to the meaning.
examples: **Yakushima is cleaned by volunteers.**
**Mt. Fuji is loved by Japanese people.**

grammarPoints.title: **Mt. Fuji will be enjoyed by people forever.**
grammarPoints.japaneseDescription: 助じょ動どう詞しつきの　受うけ身み：助じょ動どう詞しの　後うしろの　動どう詞しは　原げん形けいに　なる　ため、 助じょ動どう詞しつきの　受うけ身みの　形かたちは　〈助じょ動どう詞し＋ be ＋ 過か去こ分ぶん詞し〉と　なる。
grammarPoints.englishExplanation: When a modal verb precedes the passive structure, the modal is followed by the base form 'be', resulting in the structure 〈Modal + be + past participle〉. This allows expressing abilities, predictions, or obligations in the passive voice.
examples: **Mt. Fuji will be enjoyed by people forever.**
**Mt. Fuji can be seen in many ukiyo-e prints.**

grammarPoint.title: **I will make a reservation.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription:
助じょ動どう詞し：**will**「これから　…しよう」と　そのときに　決きめた　予よ定ていや
未み来らいの　ことを　表あらわすには　〈will ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉を　使つかう。 また、「…でしょう」「…するつもりです」など　未み来らいの

grammarPoint.englishExplanation: Use the structure 〈will + base form of the verb〉 to express a decision or plan made at the moment of speaking, referring to the immediate future, translated as 'I will do....'. examples: **You will see the sea very soon.**
**You’ll see the Merlion soon.**

exercises.question: I / will / make / a / reservation.
exercises.answer: I will make a reservation.
exercises.hint:
助じょ動どう詞し：**will**「これから　…しよう」と　そのときに　決きめた　予よ定ていや
未み来らいの　ことを　表あらわすには　〈will ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉を　使つかう。 また、「…でしょう」「…するつもりです」など　未み来らいの
予よ測そくや　意い志しを　表あらわす　ときにも　使つかう。
exercises.translation: 私は予約をします。

exercises.question: I ___ help you with your homework.
exercises.answer: will
exercises.hint: Use 'will' for a spontaneous offer.
exercises.translation: 私はあなたの宿題を手伝います。

exercises.question: It / will / be / sunny / tomorrow.
exercises.answer: It will be sunny tomorrow.
exercises.hint: It + will + be + adjective + time.
exercises.translation: 明日は晴れるでしょう。

exercises.question: I / will / call / you / later.
exercises.answer: I will call you later.
exercises.hint: I + will + verb + object + time.
exercises.translation: 後で電話します。

exercises.question: She / will / be / busy / next / week.
exercises.answer: She will be busy next week.
exercises.hint: She + will + be + adjective + time.
exercises.translation: 彼女は来週忙しくなるでしょう。

exercises.question: Will / you / open / the / window?
exercises.answer: Will you open the window?
exercises.hint: Will + you + verb...?
exercises.translation: 窓を開けてくれませんか。

exerciseSets.title: **I will show you some pictures.**
exerciseSets.topic: 文法ぶんぽう用よう語ご（文ぶん構こう造ぞう）

grammarPoint.title: **I will show you some pictures.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription:
文法ぶんぽう用よう語ご（文ぶん構こう造ぞう）：SVOO（第だい4文ぶん型けい）show, make, buy, teach, giveなど ＋ （人ひと） ＋ （もの）
「（人ひと）に　（もの）を　…する」という　意い味みに　なる。動どう詞しの
あとが、「だれ（人ひと）に ＋ 何なに（もの）を」の　順じゅん
になっていることに　注ちゅう意いする。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: This structure (Subject + Verb + Indirect Object (person) + Direct Object (thing)) means 'to do (the action) of the verb to (a person) with (a thing)'. Pay attention that the word order after the verb is always 'who (person) to whom/what (thing)'.
examples: I’ll **show you a video**.
I will **tell** my aunt **some interesting things about Singapore**.

exercises.question: I / will / show / you / some / pictures.
exercises.answer: I will show you some pictures.
exercises.hint:
文法ぶんぽう用よう語ご（文ぶん構こう造ぞう）：SVOO（第だい4文ぶん型けい）show, make, buy, teach, giveなど ＋ （人ひと） ＋ （もの）
「（人ひと）に　（もの）を　…する」という　意い味みに　なる。動どう詞しの
あとが、「だれ（人ひと）に ＋ 何なに（もの）を」の　順じゅん
になっていることに　注ちゅう意いする。
exercises.translation: 私はあなたにいくつかの写真を見せます。

exercises.question: Please ___ ___ your passport.
exercises.answer: show me
exercises.hint: show + [person]
exercises.translation: 私にあなたのパスポートを見せてください。

exercises.question: He / gave / me / a / book.
exercises.answer: He gave me a book.
exercises.hint: He + gave + [person] + [thing].
exercises.translation: 彼は私に本をくれました。

exercises.question: She / teaches / us / English.
exercises.answer: She teaches us English.
exercises.hint: She + teaches + [person] + [thing].
exercises.translation: 彼女は私たちに英語を教えています。

exercises.question: My / father / bought / me / a / bike.
exercises.answer: My father bought me a bike.
exercises.hint: My father + bought + [person] + [thing].
exercises.translation: 父は私に自転車を買ってくれました。

exercises.question: I / will / tell / you / the / truth.
exercises.answer: I will tell you the truth.
exercises.hint: I + will + tell + [person] + [thing].
exercises.translation: 私はあなたに真実を話します。

exerciseSets.title: **People call this area Little India.**
exerciseSets.topic: 文法ぶんぽう用よう語ご（文ぶん構こう造ぞう）

grammarPoint.title: **People call this area Little India.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 文法ぶんぽう用よう語ご（文ぶん構こう造ぞう）：SVOC（第だい5文ぶん型けい）2 には、動どう詞し（call）の　あとに　2つの　かたまりが　あり、our dog ＝ Pochiの　関かん係けいです。 このような　場ば合あい、our dogを　目もく的てき語ご、Pochiのほうは　補ほ語ごと　いいます。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: In this structure (Subject + Verb + Object + Complement), the verb (like 'call') is followed by two elements where the Object and the Complement are related (e.g., 'our dog' equals 'Pochi'). The second element (Complement) explains the state or condition of the Object.
examples: We **call our dog Pochi**.
We **call our dog Pochi**.

exercises.question: People / call / this / area / Little / India.
exercises.answer: People call this area Little India.
exercises.hint: 文法ぶんぽう用よう語ご（文ぶん構こう造ぞう）：SVOC（第だい5文ぶん型けい）2 には、動どう詞し（call）の　あとに　2つの　かたまりが　あり、our dog ＝ Pochiの　関かん係けいです。 このような　場ば合あい、our dogを　目もく的てき語ご、Pochiのほうは　補ほ語ごと　いいます。
exercises.translation: 人々はこの地域をリトル・インディアと呼びます。

exercises.question: They ___ the dog Pochi.
exercises.answer: call
exercises.hint: Verb for naming.
exercises.translation: 彼らはその犬をポチと呼びます。

exercises.question: We / call / him / Ken.
exercises.answer: We call him Ken.
exercises.hint: We + call + [person] + [name].
exercises.translation: 私たちは彼をケンと呼びます。

exercises.question: Please / call / me / Mike.
exercises.answer: Please call me Mike.
exercises.hint: Please + call + [person] + [name].
exercises.translation: 私をマイクと呼んでください。

exercises.question: They / named / the / baby / Sakura.
exercises.answer: They named the baby Sakura.
exercises.hint: They + named + [person] + [name].
exercises.translation: 彼らはその赤ちゃんをサクラと名付けました。

exercises.question: What / do / you / call / this / in / English?
exercises.answer: What do you call this in English?
exercises.hint: What + do + you + call + [thing]...?
exercises.translation: これは英語で何と呼びますか。

exerciseSets.title: **When I go to a ramen restaurant, I order tonkotsu ramen.**
exerciseSets.topic: 接せつ続ぞく詞し

grammarPoint.title: **When I go to a ramen restaurant, I order tonkotsu ramen.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription:
接せつ続ぞく詞し：**when**when ...は、「…（の）
ときに」という　意い味みに なる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The subordinating conjunction 'when' is used to connect two clauses and means 'at the time when...'. The 'when' clause can appear at the start or end of the sentence. If placed first, use a comma before the main clause.
examples: **When I eat breakfast, I watch the news on TV.**
**I order tonkotsu ramen when I go to a ramen restaurant.**

exercises.question: When / I / go / to / a / ramen / restaurant, / I / order / tonkotsu / ramen.
exercises.answer: When I go to a ramen restaurant, I order tonkotsu ramen.
exercises.hint:
接せつ続ぞく詞し：**when**when ...は、「…（の）
ときに」という　意い味みに なる。
exercises.translation: ラーメン屋に行くとき、私は豚骨ラーメンを注文します。

exercises.question: ___ I get home, I wash my hands.
exercises.answer: When
exercises.hint: Time word.
exercises.translation: 家に帰るとき、私は手を洗います。

exercises.question: I / watch / TV / when / I / have / time.
exercises.answer: I watch TV when I have time.
exercises.hint: I + watch + TV + when + I + have + time.
exercises.translation: 時間があるとき、私はテレビを見ます。

exercises.question: When / he / came / home, / I / was / sleeping.
exercises.answer: When he came home, I was sleeping.
exercises.hint: When + he + came + home, + I + was + sleeping.
exercises.translation: 彼が帰宅したとき、私は眠っていました。

exercises.question: Please / call / me / when / you / arrive.
exercises.answer: Please call me when you arrive.
exercises.hint: Please + call + me + when + you + arrive.
exercises.translation: 到着したら電話してください。

exercises.question: When / I / was / a / child, / I / lived / in / Tokyo.
exercises.answer: When I was a child, I lived in Tokyo.
exercises.hint: When + I + was + a + child...
exercises.translation: 私が子供だった頃、東京に住んでいました。

exerciseSets.title: **If you have time, you can come.**
exerciseSets.topic: 接せつ続ぞく詞し

grammarPoint.title: **If you have time, you can come.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 接せつ続ぞく詞し：**if**「（もし）…ならば」と　条じょう件けんを　表あらわすには、ifを　使つかう。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The conjunction 'if' is used to express a condition, meaning '(If)... then...'. Note that even when referring to a future condition, the verb following 'if' must be in the present tense.
examples: **If you love ramen, I’ll tell you about some good restaurants.**
**You can come if you have time.**

exercises.question: If / you / have / time, / you / can / come.
exercises.answer: If you have time, you can come.
exercises.hint: 接せつ続ぞく詞し：**if**「（もし）…ならば」と　条じょう件けんを　表あらわすには、ifを　使つかう。
exercises.translation: もし時間があれば、来てもいいですよ。

exercises.question: ___ you are busy, I will go alone.
exercises.answer: If
exercises.hint: Condition word.
exercises.translation: もしあなたが忙しいなら、私は一人で行きます。

exercises.question: I / will / stay / home / if / it / rains.
exercises.answer: I will stay home if it rains.
exercises.hint: I + will + stay + home + if + it + rains.
exercises.translation: もし雨が降ったら、私は家にいます。

exercises.question: If / you / are / hungry, / eat / this / apple.
exercises.answer: If you are hungry, eat this apple.
exercises.hint: If + you + are + hungry, + eat + this + apple.
exercises.translation: もしお腹が空いているなら、このリンゴを食べなさい。

exercises.question: Please / ask / me / if / you / have / any / questions.
exercises.answer: Please ask me if you have any questions.
exercises.hint: Please + ask + me + if + you + have + any + questions.
exercises.translation: もし質問があれば、私に聞いてください。

exercises.question: If / you / like / soccer, / let's / play / together.
exercises.answer: If you like soccer, let's play together.
exercises.hint: If + you + like + soccer...
exercises.translation: もしサッカーが好きなら、一緒にしましょう。

exerciseSets.title: **I like Sapporo ramen because the soup is thick.**
exerciseSets.topic: 接せつ続ぞく詞し

grammarPoint.title: **I like Sapporo ramen because the soup is thick.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 接せつ続ぞく詞し：**because**「（なぜなら）…だから」と 理り由ゆうを　表あらわすには、becauseを　使つかう。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The conjunction 'because' is used to state a reason, meaning '(because)... therefore'. The 'because' clause can appear at the start or end of the sentence. If placed first, use a comma before the main clause.
examples: **I enjoy Japanese sweets because they look beautiful.**
**Because the soup is thick, I like Sapporo ramen.**

exercises.question: I / like / Sapporo / ramen / because / the / soup / is / thick.
exercises.answer: I like Sapporo ramen because the soup is thick.
exercises.hint: 接せつ続ぞく詞し：**because**「（なぜなら）…だから」と 理り由ゆうを　表あらわすには、becauseを　使つかう。
exercises.translation: スープが濃厚なので、私は札幌ラーメンが好きです。

exercises.question: She is happy ___ she passed the test.
exercises.answer: because
exercises.hint: Reason word.
exercises.translation: 彼女は試験に合格したので幸せです。

exercises.question: He / is / popular / because / he / is / kind.
exercises.answer: He is popular because he is kind.
exercises.hint: He + is + popular + because + he + is + kind.
exercises.translation: 彼は親切なので人気があります。

exercises.question: I / went / to / bed / early / because / I / was / tired.
exercises.answer: I went to bed early because I was tired.
exercises.hint: I + went + to + bed + early + because + I + was + tired.
exercises.translation: 私は疲れていたので早く寝ました。

exercises.question: Because / it / was / raining, / we / stayed / inside.
exercises.answer: Because it was raining, we stayed inside.
exercises.hint: Because + it + was + raining...
exercises.translation: 雨が降っていたので、私たちは中にいました。

exercises.question: I / study / English / because / I / want / to / travel.
exercises.answer: I study English because I want to travel.
exercises.hint: I + study + English + because...
exercises.translation: 旅行したいので、私は英語を勉強しています。

exerciseSets.title: **I think (that) food travels around the world.**
exerciseSets.topic: 接せつ続ぞく詞し

grammarPoint.title: **I think (that) food travels around the world.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription:
接せつ続ぞく詞し：**that**think (that) ...は、「…と　思おもう」という　意い味みに　なる。thatは　省しょう略りゃくされる　ことが　多おお
い。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The structure 'think (that)...' means 'I believe that...' or 'I am of the opinion that...'. The word 'that' introduces a noun clause that acts as the object of the verb 'think', and it is often omitted in casual speech or writing.
examples: **Eddy thinks (that) food culture is always changing.**
**I think chefs use local ingredients in ramen.**

exercises.question: I / think / (that) / food / travels / around / the / world.
exercises.answer: I think (that) food travels around the world.
exercises.hint:
接せつ続ぞく詞し：**that**think (that) ...は、「…と　思おもう」という　意い味みに　なる。thatは　省しょう略りゃくされる　ことが　多おお
い。
exercises.translation: 私は食は世界中を旅すると思います。

exercises.question: I ___ this book is interesting.
exercises.answer: think
exercises.hint: Opinion verb.
exercises.translation: 私はこの本は面白いと思います。

exercises.question: I / think / that / English / is / important.
exercises.answer: I think that English is important.
exercises.hint: I + think + that + English + is + important.
exercises.translation: 私は英語は重要だと思います。

exercises.question: Do / you / think / that / he / is / busy?
exercises.answer: Do you think that he is busy?
exercises.hint: Do + you + think + that + he + is + busy?
exercises.translation: あなたは彼は忙しいと思いますか。

exercises.question: I / don't / think / that / it / is / true.
exercises.answer: I don't think that it is true.
exercises.hint: I + don't + think + that + it + is + true.
exercises.translation: 私はそれが本当だとは思いません。

exercises.question: She / thinks / that / cats / are / cute.
exercises.answer: She thinks that cats are cute.
exercises.hint: She + thinks + that + cats + are + cute.
exercises.translation: 彼女は猫は可愛いと思っています。

exerciseSets.title: **I use a computer to study English.**
exerciseSets.topic: 不ふ定てい詞し（副ふく詞してき用よう法ほう）, 不ふ定てい詞し（原げん因いんを　表あらわす　副ふく詞してき用よう法ほう）

grammarPoint.title: **I use a computer to study English.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription:
不ふ定てい詞し（副ふく詞してき用よう法ほう）：「…する　ために」という　意い味みを
表あらわすには、 〈to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉を　使つかう。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: Use the infinitive phrase 〈to + base form of the verb〉 to express purpose, meaning 'in order to...' or 'to do...'. This phrase functions adverbially, modifying the main verb.
examples: **I went to a bookstore to look for interesting comic books.**
**I got up early to see the new movie.**

exercises.question: I / use / a / computer / to / study / English.
exercises.answer: I use a computer to study English.
exercises.hint:
不ふ定てい詞し（副ふく詞してき用よう法ほう）：「…する　ために」という　意い味みを
表あらわすには、 〈to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉を　使つかう。
exercises.translation: 私は英語を勉強するためにコンピュータを使います。

exercises.question: I went to the park ___ play soccer.
exercises.answer: to
exercises.hint: Infinitive marker.
exercises.translation: 私はサッカーをするために公園に行きました。

exercises.question: He / studies / hard / to / be / a / doctor.
exercises.answer: He studies hard to be a doctor.
exercises.hint: He + studies + hard + to + be + a + doctor.
exercises.translation: 彼は医者になるために一生懸命勉強しています。

exercises.question: We / visited / Kyoto / to / see / old / temples.
exercises.answer: We visited Kyoto to see old temples.
exercises.hint: We + visited + Kyoto + to + see + old + temples.
exercises.translation: 私たちは古いお寺を見るために京都を訪れました。

exercises.question: I / got / up / early / to / run.
exercises.answer: I got up early to run.
exercises.hint: I + got + up + early + to + run.
exercises.translation: 私は走るために早く起きました。

exercises.question: She / came / here / to / help / us.
exercises.answer: She came here to help us.
exercises.hint: She + came + here + to + help + us.
exercises.translation: 彼女は私たちを手伝うためにここに来ました。

exerciseSets.title: **I am happy to hear that.**
exerciseSets.topic: 不ふ定てい詞し（副ふく詞してき用よう法ほう）, 不ふ定てい詞し（原げん因いんを　表あらわす　副ふく詞してき用よう法ほう）

grammarPoint.title: **I am happy to hear that.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription:
不ふ定てい詞し（原げん因いんを　表あらわす　副ふく詞してき用よう法ほう）：〈to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉が、「…して」（感かん情じょうの　原げん因いんを　表あらわす）の　意い味みに
なる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The infinitive phrase 〈to + base form of the verb〉 can follow adjectives expressing emotion (like happy, surprised, sad) to indicate the cause or reason for that emotion, meaning 'I am (emotion) because of/to....'
examples: **I’m excited to go to a car factory.**
**I was glad to see their happy faces.**

exercises.question: I / am / happy / to / hear / that.
exercises.answer: I am happy to hear that.
exercises.hint:
不ふ定てい詞し（原げん因いんを　表あらわす　副ふく詞してき用よう法ほう）：〈to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉が、「…して」（感かん情じょうの　原げん因いんを　表あらわす）の　意い味みに
なる。
exercises.translation: 私はそれを聞いてうれしいです。

exercises.question: I am glad ___ see you.
exercises.answer: to
exercises.hint: Infinitive marker.
exercises.translation: 私はあなたに会えてうれしいです。

exercises.question: She / was / sad / to / hear / the / news.
exercises.answer: She was sad to hear the news.
exercises.hint: She + was + sad + to + hear + the + news.
exercises.translation: 彼女はその知らせを聞いて悲しかったです。

exercises.question: I / am / surprised / to / see / you / here.
exercises.answer: I am surprised to see you here.
exercises.hint: I + am + surprised + to + see + you + here.
exercises.translation: 私はここであなたに会って驚いています。

exercises.question: We / are / sorry / to / hear / that.
exercises.answer: We are sorry to hear that.
exercises.hint: We + are + sorry + to + hear + that.
exercises.translation: 私たちはそれを聞いて残念です。

exercises.question: He / was / excited / to / go / to / the / zoo.
exercises.answer: He was excited to go to the zoo.
exercises.hint: He + was + excited + to + go + to + the + zoo.
exercises.translation: 彼は動物園に行けるので興奮していました。

exerciseSets.title: **She has a lot of work to do.**
exerciseSets.topic: 不ふ定てい詞し（形けい容よう詞してき用よう法ほう）

grammarPoint.title: **She has a lot of work to do.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription:
不ふ定てい詞し（形けい容よう詞してき用よう法ほう）：〈to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉が　すぐ前まえの　（代だい）名めい詞しを　修しゅう飾しょくして　説せつ明めいを　加くわえ、「…すべき」
「…する　ための」という　意い味みに　なる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The infinitive phrase 〈to + base form of the verb〉 modifies the preceding (pro)noun, functioning adjectivally. It means 'work to be done' or 'things needed to...'
examples: **I have various things to study.**
**Asakusa is the place to visit.**

exercises.question: She / has / a / lot / of / work / to / do.
exercises.answer: She has a lot of work to do.
exercises.hint:
不ふ定てい詞し（形けい容よう詞してき用よう法ほう）：〈to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉が　すぐ前まえの　（代だい）名めい詞しを　修しゅう飾しょくして　説せつ明めいを　加くわえ、「…すべき」
「…する　ための」という　意い味みに　なる。
exercises.translation: 彼女にはすべき仕事がたくさんあります。

exercises.question: I have no time ___ watch TV.
exercises.answer: to
exercises.hint: Infinitive marker.
exercises.translation: 私にはテレビを見る時間がありません。

exercises.question: Do / you / have / anything / to / drink?
exercises.answer: Do you have anything to drink?
exercises.hint: Do + you + have + anything + to + drink?
exercises.translation: 何か飲み物はありますか。

exercises.question: I / want / something / cold / to / drink.
exercises.answer: I want something cold to drink.
exercises.hint: I + want + something + cold + to + drink.
exercises.translation: 私は何か冷たい飲み物が欲しいです。

exercises.question: There / are / many / places / to / visit / in / Kyoto.
exercises.answer: There are many places to visit in Kyoto.
exercises.hint: There + are + many + places + to + visit + in + Kyoto.
exercises.translation: 京都には訪れるべき場所がたくさんあります。

exercises.question: He / has / a / promise / to / keep.
exercises.answer: He has a promise to keep.
exercises.hint: He + has + a + promise + to + keep.
exercises.translation: 彼には守るべき約束があります。

exerciseSets.title: **It is important to look at the children’s faces.**
exerciseSets.topic: 不ふ定てい詞し（名めい詞してき用よう法ほう）

grammarPoint.title: **It is important to look at the children’s faces.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 不ふ定てい詞し（名めい詞してき用よう法ほう）：It is ... ＋ to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい「～するのは　…です」という　意い味みに　なる。この　itは、to以い下の　内ない容ようを　示しめす。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: This structure uses the indefinite pronoun 'It' as a temporary subject, and the infinitive phrase (to + base form of the verb) provides the real subject, meaning 'To do (action) is (adjective)'. This is used to state that performing an action is necessary or noteworthy.
examples: **It is necessary to watch the children carefully.**
**It is interesting to learn English.**

exercises.question: It / is / important / to / look / at / the / children’s / faces.
exercises.answer: It is important to look at the children’s faces.
exercises.hint: 不ふ定てい詞し（名めい詞してき用よう法ほう）：It is ... ＋ to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい「～するのは　…です」という　意い味みに　なる。この　itは、to以い下の　内ない容ようを　示しめす。
exercises.translation: 子供たちの顔を見ることは重要です。

exercises.question: It is fun ___ play tennis.
exercises.answer: to
exercises.hint: Infinitive marker.
exercises.translation: テニスをするのは楽しいです。

exercises.question: It / is / difficult / to / speak / English.
exercises.answer: It is difficult to speak English.
exercises.hint: It + is + difficult + to + speak + English.
exercises.translation: 英語を話すのは難しいです。

exercises.question: It / is / easy / for / me / to / read / this / book.
exercises.answer: It is easy for me to read this book.
exercises.hint: It + is + easy + for + me + to + read + this + book.
exercises.translation: 私にとってこの本を読むのは簡単です。

exercises.question: It / is / interesting / to / learn / about / history.
exercises.answer: It is interesting to learn about history.
exercises.hint: It + is + interesting + to + learn + about + history.
exercises.translation: 歴史について学ぶのは面白いです。

exercises.question: It / is / necessary / to / sleep / well.

exercises.hint: It + is + necessary + to + sleep + well.
exercises.translation: よく眠ることは必要です。

exerciseSets.title: **You have to speak English. You do not have to speak perfect English.**
exerciseSets.topic: 文法ぶんぽう用よう語ご（助じょ動どう詞し）, 助じょ動どう詞し

grammarPoint.title: **You have to speak English. You do not have to speak perfect English.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 文法ぶんぽう用よう語ご（助じょ動どう詞し）：**have to**＋動どう詞しの原げん形けい「…しなければならない」と　必ひつ要よう性せいや　義ぎ務むを表あらわすには、〈have to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉を　使つかう。否ひ定てい文ぶんでは、「…しなくて　よい」という　意い味みになる。主しゅ語ごが　三人にん称しょう　単たん数すうの　ときは、has to、does not have toと　なる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The structure 〈have to + base form of the verb〉 expresses necessity or obligation, meaning 'must' or 'need to'. In the negative form, 'do not have to' (or 'does not have to' for third person singular), it means 'it is not necessary to...', or 'do not need to...'
examples: **We have to bring our lunch.**
**I don’t have to take a map.**

exercises.question: You / have / to / speak / English.
exercises.answer: You have to speak English.
exercises.hint: 文法ぶんぽう用よう語ご（助じょ動どう詞し）：**have to**＋動どう詞しの原げん形けい「…しなければならない」と　必ひつ要よう性せいや　義ぎ務むを表あらわすには、〈have to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉を　使つかう。否ひ定てい文ぶんでは、「…しなくて　よい」という　意い味みになる。主しゅ語ごが　三人にん称しょう　単たん数すうの　ときは、has to、does not have toと　なる。
exercises.translation: あなたは英語を話さなければなりません。

exercises.question: I ___ ___ go now.
exercises.answer: have to
exercises.hint: Phrase meaning 'must'.
exercises.translation: 私は今行かなければなりません。

exercises.question: She / has / to / study / math.
exercises.answer: She has to study math.
exercises.hint: She + has + to + study + math.
exercises.translation: 彼女は数学を勉強しなければなりません。

exercises.question: You / don't / have / to / hurry.
exercises.answer: You don't have to hurry.
exercises.hint: You + don't + have + to + hurry.
exercises.translation: あなたは急ぐ必要はありません。

exercises.question: Do / I / have / to / clean / my / room?
exercises.answer: Do I have to clean my room?
exercises.hint: Do + I + have + to + clean + my + room?
exercises.translation: 私は部屋を掃除しなければなりませんか。

exercises.question: He / doesn't / have / to / come.
exercises.answer: He doesn't have to come.
exercises.hint: He + doesn't + have + to + come.
exercises.translation: 彼は来る必要はありません。

exerciseSets.title: **We must save water. We must not take long showers.**
exerciseSets.topic: 文法ぶんぽう用よう語ご（助じょ動どう詞し）, 助じょ動どう詞し

grammarPoint.title: **We must save water. We must not take long showers.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription:
助じょ動どう詞し：**must**「…しなければならない」と　義ぎ務むや　命めい令れいを
表あらわすには、〈must ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉を　使つかう。 否ひ定てい文ぶんでは、「…してはならない」と　禁きん止しを
表あらわす。短たん縮しゅく形けいは　mustn’tと　なる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The structure 〈must + base form of the verb〉 expresses strong obligation or command, meaning 'it is absolutely necessary to...'. In the negative form, 'must not' (or 'mustn’t'), it expresses prohibition, meaning 'must not do...'
examples: **You must stay with us.**
**You must not make a fire.**

exercises.question: We / must / save / water.
exercises.answer: We must save water.
exercises.hint:
助じょ動どう詞し：**must**「…しなければならない」と　義ぎ務むや　命めい令れいを
表あらわすには、〈must ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉を　使つかう。 否ひ定てい文ぶんでは、「…してはならない」と　禁きん止しを
表あらわす。短たん縮しゅく形けいは　mustn’tと　なる。
exercises.translation: 私たちは水を節約しなければなりません。

exercises.question: You ___ not run here.
exercises.answer: must
exercises.hint: Strong prohibition.
exercises.translation: ここで走ってはいけません。

exercises.question: We / must / not / take / long / showers.
exercises.answer: We must not take long showers.
exercises.hint: We + must + not + take + long + showers.
exercises.translation: 私たちは長いシャワーを浴びてはいけません。

exercises.question: I / must / finish / my / homework.
exercises.answer: I must finish my homework.
exercises.hint: I + must + finish + my + homework.
exercises.translation: 私は宿題を終わらせなければなりません。

exercises.question: You / must / be / quiet / in / the / library.
exercises.answer: You must be quiet in the library.
exercises.hint: You + must + be + quiet + in + the + library.
exercises.translation: 図書館では静かにしなければなりません。

exercises.question: He / must / go / to / the / hospital.
exercises.answer: He must go to the hospital.
exercises.hint: He + must + go + to + the + hospital.
exercises.translation: 彼は病院に行かなければなりません。

exerciseSets.title: **They enjoy reading books.**
exerciseSets.topic: 動どう名めい詞し

grammarPoint.title: **They enjoy reading books.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 動どう名めい詞し：動どう詞しに　ingが　ついた　形かたちは、進しん行こう形けいで　使つかう　ほかにも、「…すること」という　名めい詞しの　働はたらきを　する。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The -ing form added to a verb (gerund) functions as a noun, meaning 'the act of doing...'. It is used here as the object of a verb like 'enjoy'.
examples: **They finished eating lunch.**
**I enjoy swimming in the sea.**

exercises.question: They / enjoy / reading / books.
exercises.answer: They enjoy reading books.
exercises.hint: 動どう名めい詞し：動どう詞しに　ingが　ついた　形かたちは、進しん行こう形けいで　使つかう　ほかにも、「…すること」という　名めい詞しの　働はたらきを　する。
exercises.translation: 彼らは読書を楽しみます。

exercises.question: I finished ___ lunch.
exercises.answer: eating
exercises.hint: Gerund form of 'eat'.
exercises.translation: 私は昼食を食べ終わりました。

exercises.question: Stop / talking.
exercises.answer: Stop talking.
exercises.hint: Stop + verb-ing.
exercises.translation: 話すのをやめなさい。

exercises.question: He / likes / playing / soccer.
exercises.answer: He likes playing soccer.
exercises.hint: He + likes + playing + soccer.
exercises.translation: 彼はサッカーをするのが好きです。

exercises.question: She / started / learning / English.
exercises.answer: She started learning English.
exercises.hint: She + started + learning + English.
exercises.translation: 彼女は英語を学び始めました。

exercises.question: We / enjoyed / swimming / in / the / sea.
exercises.answer: We enjoyed swimming in the sea.
exercises.hint: We + enjoyed + swimming + in + the + sea.
exercises.translation: 私たちは海で泳ぐのを楽しみました。

exerciseSets.title: **Talking with him was fun.**
exerciseSets.topic: 動どう名めい詞し

grammarPoint.title: **Talking with him was fun.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription:
動どう名めい詞し：動どう詞しに　ingが　ついた　形かたち（「…すること」）を　主しゅ語ごとして　使つかう
ことも　できる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The -ing form added to a verb (gerund) can function as the subject of a sentence, meaning 'The act of doing...' is/was (adjective). When used as a subject, it takes the singular form of the verb (is/was).
examples: **Walking together was nice.**
**Taking pictures of animals is interesting.**

exercises.question: Talking / with / him / was / fun.
exercises.answer: Talking with him was fun.
exercises.hint:
動どう名めい詞し：動どう詞しに　ingが　ついた　形かたち（「…すること」）を　主しゅ語ごとして　使つかう
ことも　できる。
exercises.translation: 彼と話すのは楽しかったです。

exercises.question: ___ soccer is exciting.
exercises.answer: Playing
exercises.hint: Gerund form of 'play'.
exercises.translation: サッカーをするのはワクワクします。

exercises.question: Learning / English / is / important.
exercises.answer: Learning English is important.
exercises.hint: Learning + English + is + important.
exercises.translation: 英語を学ぶことは重要です。

exercises.question: Listening / to / music / is / my / hobby.
exercises.answer: Listening to music is my hobby.
exercises.hint: Listening + to + music + is + my + hobby.
exercises.translation: 音楽を聴くことは私の趣味です。

exercises.question: Getting / up / early / is / good / for / your / health.
exercises.answer: Getting up early is good for your health.
exercises.hint: Getting + up + early + is + good + for + your + health.
exercises.translation: 早起きは健康に良いです。

exercises.question: Eating / vegetables / is / necessary.
exercises.answer: Eating vegetables is necessary.
exercises.hint: Eating + vegetables + is + necessary.
exercises.translation: 野菜を食べることは必要です。

exerciseSets.title: **I know how to use these products.**
exerciseSets.topic: 疑ぎ問もん詞し ＋ to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい, 主しゅ語ご ＋ 動どう詞し ＋（人ひと）＋ 疑ぎ問もん詞し ＋ to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい

grammarPoint.title: **I know how to use these products.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 疑ぎ問もん詞し ＋ to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい：howや　whatの　あとに　〈to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉が　続つづくと、「どのように　…するか」「何なにを　…すべきか」という　意い味みに　なる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The structure of an interrogative word (like how, what, where) followed by 〈to + base form of the verb〉 functions nominally, meaning 'how to do...', 'what to do...', or 'where to find...'. This phrase usually acts as the object of the main verb.
examples: **Anna knows when to leave her house.**
**I can tell you where to find facilities with a universal design in our city, if you want.**

exercises.question: I / know / how / to / use / these / products.
exercises.answer: I know how to use these products.
exercises.hint: 疑ぎ問もん詞し ＋ to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい：howや　whatの　あとに　〈to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい〉が　続つづくと、「どのように　…するか」「何なにを　…すべきか」という　意い味みに　なる。
exercises.translation: 私はこれらの製品の使い方を知っています。

exercises.question: Please tell me ___ ___ do.
exercises.answer: what to
exercises.hint: Phrase meaning 'the thing which I should do'.
exercises.translation: 何をするべきか教えてください。

exercises.question: I / don't / know / where / to / go.
exercises.answer: I don't know where to go.
exercises.hint: I + don't + know + where + to + go.
exercises.translation: 私はどこへ行けばよいかわかりません。

exercises.question: He / knows / when / to / start.
exercises.answer: He knows when to start.
exercises.hint: He + knows + when + to + start.
exercises.translation: 彼はいつ始めるべきか知っています。

exercises.question: Do / you / know / how / to / swim?
exercises.answer: Do you know how to swim?
exercises.hint: Do + you + know + how + to + swim?
exercises.translation: あなたは泳ぎ方を知っていますか。

exercises.question: They / are / discussing / what / to / buy.
exercises.answer: They are discussing what to buy.
exercises.hint: They + are + discussing + what + to + buy.
exercises.translation: 彼らは何を買うべきか話し合っています。

exerciseSets.title: **I can show you how to use these products.**
exerciseSets.topic: 疑ぎ問もん詞し ＋ to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい, 主しゅ語ご ＋ 動どう詞し ＋（人ひと）＋ 疑ぎ問もん詞し ＋ to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい

grammarPoint.title: **I can show you how to use these products.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 主しゅ語ご ＋ 動どう詞し ＋（人ひと）＋ 疑ぎ問もん詞し ＋ to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい：「（人ひと）に（どのように　…するか）を　～する」と いう　意い味みに　なる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: This structure involves a verb that takes both an indirect object (person) and a complex object (interrogative + infinitive phrase). It means 'I can show (a person) how to do (an action)' or 'I can tell (a person) where to find (something)'.
examples: **I can tell you how to use these scissors.**
**I will show you where to find accessible restrooms.**

exercises.question: I / can / show / you / how / to / use / these / products.
exercises.answer: I can show you how to use these products.
exercises.hint: 主しゅ語ご ＋ 動どう詞し ＋（人ひと）＋ 疑ぎ問もん詞し ＋ to ＋ 動どう詞しの原げん形けい：「（人ひと）に（どのように　…するか）を　～する」と いう　意い味みに　なる。
exercises.translation: 私はあなたにこれらの製品の使い方を見せることができます。

exercises.question: Please tell me ___ ___ get to the station.
exercises.answer: how to
exercises.hint: Phrase meaning 'the way to'.
exercises.translation: 駅への行き方を教えてください。

exercises.question: She / taught / us / what / to / study.
exercises.answer: She taught us what to study.
exercises.hint: She + taught + us + what + to + study.
exercises.translation: 彼女は私たちに何を勉強すべきか教えてくれました。

exercises.question: I / will / show / you / where / to / park.
exercises.answer: I will show you where to park.
exercises.hint: I + will + show + you + where + to + park.
exercises.translation: どこに駐車すべきか案内します。

exercises.question: Can / you / tell / me / when / to / come?
exercises.answer: Can you tell me when to come?
exercises.hint: Can + you + tell + me + when + to + come?
exercises.translation: いつ来ればよいか教えてくれますか。

exercises.question: He / asked / me / how / to / make / a / cake.
exercises.answer: He asked me how to make a cake.
exercises.hint: He + asked + me + how + to + make + a + cake.
exercises.translation: 彼は私にケーキの作り方を尋ねました。

exerciseSets.title: **I am sure that these ideas help many people.**
exerciseSets.topic: 主しゅ語ご ＋ be動どう詞し ＋ 形けい容よう詞し ＋ that感かん情じょうや　心しん理り　を表あらわす　形けい容よう詞しの　あとに　that ...を 続つづけると、「きっと　…だ」「…して　うれしい」などという　意い味みに　なる。

grammarPoint.title: **I am sure that these ideas help many people.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 主しゅ語ご ＋ be動どう詞し ＋ 形けい容よう詞し ＋ that感かん情じょうや　心しん理り　を表あらわす　形けい容よう詞しの　あとに　that ...を 続つづけると、「きっと　…だ」「…して　うれしい」などという　意い味みに　なる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: When an adjective expressing feeling or mental state (like sure, glad) is followed by a 'that' clause, it means 'I am certain that...' or 'I am happy that...'. This structure clearly states the speaker's conviction or emotion regarding the following clause.
examples: **I think the ramp is great.**
**I am glad that you became interested in universal design.**

exercises.question: I / am / sure / that / these / ideas / help / many / people.
exercises.answer: I am sure that these ideas help many people.
exercises.hint: 主しゅ語ご ＋ be動どう詞し ＋ 形けい容よう詞し ＋ that感かん情じょうや　心しん理り　を表あらわす　形けい容よう詞しの　あとに　that ...を 続つづけると、「きっと　…だ」「…して　うれしい」などという　意い味みに　なる。
exercises.translation: これらのアイデアが多くの人々を助けると確信しています。

exercises.question: I am ___ that you are here.
exercises.answer: glad
exercises.hint: Adjective meaning 'happy'.
exercises.translation: あなたがここにいてくれて嬉しいです。

exercises.question: I / am / afraid / that / I / can't / go.
exercises.answer: I am afraid that I can't go.
exercises.hint: I + am + afraid + that + I + can't + go.
exercises.translation: 残念ながら私は行けません。

exercises.question: We / are / sorry / that / we / are / late.
exercises.answer: We are sorry that we are late.
exercises.hint: We + are + sorry + that + we + are + late.
exercises.translation: 遅れてすみません。

exercises.question: She / is / sure / that / he / will / win.

exercises.hint: She + is + sure + that + he + will + win.
exercises.translation: 彼女は彼が勝つと確信しています。

exercises.question: I / am / surprised / that / the / news / is / true.
exercises.answer: I am surprised that the news is true.
exercises.hint: I + am + surprised + that + the + news + is + true.
exercises.translation: そのニュースが本当だとは驚きです。

exerciseSets.title: **A volleyball is smaller than a basketball. A volleyball is the smallest of the three.**
exerciseSets.topic: 比較ひかく級きゅう、最さい上じょう級きゅう

grammarPoint.title: **A volleyball is smaller than a basketball. A volleyball is the smallest of the three.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription:
比較ひかく級きゅう、最さい上じょう級きゅう：２つの　ものを　比くらべて　「～よりも…」と　言いう　ときは　比較ひかく級きゅう（...er）を　使つかう。３つ以い上じょうの　ものを　比くらべて　「いちばん…」と　言いう
ときは　〈the ＋ 最さい上じょう級きゅう（...est）〉を　使つかう。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: To compare two items, use the comparative form (-er, followed by 'than') meaning 'more/less than...'. To compare three or more items, use the superlative form (the -est), meaning 'the most/least... of all'.
examples: **A basketball is bigger than a tennis ball.**
**A tennis ball is the smallest of the five.**

exercises.question: A / volleyball / is / smaller / than / a / basketball.
exercises.answer: A volleyball is smaller than a basketball.
exercises.hint:
比較ひかく級きゅう、最さい上じょう級きゅう：２つの　ものを　比くらべて　「～よりも…」と　言いう　ときは　比較ひかく級きゅう（...er）を　使つかう。３つ以い上じょうの　ものを　比くらべて　「いちばん…」と　言いう
ときは　〈the ＋ 最さい上じょう級きゅう（...est）〉を　使つかう。
exercises.translation: バレーボールはバスケットボールより小さいです。

exercises.question: A / volleyball / is / the / smallest / of / the / three.
exercises.answer: A volleyball is the smallest of the three.
exercises.hint: A + volleyball + is + the + smallest + of + the + three.
exercises.translation: バレーボールはその3つの中で一番小さいです。

exercises.question: This bag is ___ than that one.
exercises.answer: heavier
exercises.hint: Comparative form of 'heavy'.
exercises.translation: この鞄はあの鞄より重いです。

exercises.question: He / is / taller / than / me.
exercises.answer: He is taller than me.
exercises.hint: He + is + taller + than + me.
exercises.translation: 彼は私より背が高いです。

exercises.question: This / is / the / biggest / apple / of / all.
exercises.answer: This is the biggest apple of all.

exerciseSets.topic: 比較ひかく級きゅう、最さい上じょう級きゅう

grammarPoint.title: **This sport is more interesting than that one. This sport is the most interesting sport of all.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription:
比較ひかく級きゅう、最さい上じょう級きゅう：比較ひかく的てきつづりの　長ながい　形けい容よう詞しや
副ふく詞しの　場ば合あい、比較ひかく級きゅうは　more ...、
最さい上じょう級きゅうは　most ...と　なる。
最さい上じょう級きゅうには　theを　つける。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: For adjectives or adverbs with longer spellings (typically three or more syllables), the comparative form uses 'more...' (followed by 'than'), and the superlative form uses 'the most...'. Remember to use 'the' with the superlative form.
examples: **This sport is more exciting than that one.**
**Soccer is the most exciting sport of all.**

副ふく詞しの　場ば合あい、比較ひかく級きゅうは　more ...、
最さい上じょう級きゅうは　most ...と　なる。
最さい上じょう級きゅうには　theを　つける。
exercises.translation: このスポーツはあのスポーツより面白いです。

exerciseSets.title: **Many of our classmates like other sports better than basketball. Seven of them like tennis the best.**
exerciseSets.topic: betterと best

grammarPoint.title: **Many of our classmates like other sports better than basketball. Seven of them like tennis the best.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: betterと best：goodや　well、very muchの　場ば合あい、比較ひかく級きゅうは　better、 最さい上じょう級きゅうは　bestと　なる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The irregular comparative form of 'good' (adjective), 'well' (adverb), and 'like... very much' (idiom) is 'better', and the superlative form is 'best'. These irregular forms do not follow the standard -er/-est or more/most patterns.
examples: **I like English the best of all subjects.**
**I like pizza better than sushi.**

exerciseSets.title: **Soccer is as popular as tennis.**
exerciseSets.topic: as ＋ 原げん級きゅう ＋ as

grammarPoint.title: **Soccer is as popular as tennis.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription:
as ＋ 原げん級きゅう ＋ as：as ... as ～は　「～と　同おなじくらい…」、not as ... as ～では
「～ほど…ではない」という　意い味みに　なる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The phrase 'as ... as ~' is used to show that two things are equal in degree regarding the adjective or adverb used, meaning 'the same degree of... as...'. The phrase 'not as ... as ~' means 'not to the same degree as...'
examples: **Your presentation was as good as Riko’s.**
**Pandas are as cute as rabbits.**

exercises.hint:

「～ほど…ではない」という　意い味みに　なる。
exercises.translation: サッカーはテニスと同じくらい人気があります。

exerciseSets.title: **This place is selected as a World Heritage site.**
exerciseSets.topic: 受うけ身み, 受うけ身みの　疑ぎ問もん文ぶん

grammarPoint.title: **This place is selected as a World Heritage site.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 受うけ身み：「…されます」、「…されています」と　言いう　ときは、〈be動どう詞し＋ 過か去こ分ぶん詞し〉で 表あらわす。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: The passive voice uses the structure 〈be verb + past participle〉 to express an action done to the subject ('...is/are done', '...has been done'). It shifts the focus to the receiver of the action rather than the actor.
examples: **Was this shirt made in South Africa?**
**It is called the Cape Floral Region.**

exerciseSets.title: **Is it called the Cape Floral Region? ―Yes, it is. [No, it is not.]**

grammarPoint.title: **Is it called the Cape Floral Region? ―Yes, it is. [No, it is not.]**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 受うけ身みの　疑ぎ問もん文ぶん：受うけ身みの　疑ぎ問もん文ぶんでは、be動どう詞しを　主しゅ語ごの　前まえに　置おく。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: To form a question in the passive voice, place the appropriate 'be' verb (is, are, was, were) before the subject. The main verb remains in the past participle form.
examples: **Is it called the Cape Floral Region?**
**Is this stadium used for rugby matches?**

exerciseSets.title: **The Taj Mahal is loved by many people.**
exerciseSets.topic: byつきの　受うけ身み

grammarPoint.title: **The Taj Mahal is loved by many people.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: byつきの　受うけ身み：受うけ身みに　by ...が　つくと、「…によって」という　意い味みに　なる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: When the passive voice includes the phrase 'by...', it identifies the agent—the person or thing performing the action. This translates to '...is done by...'. This is used when the actor is important to the meaning.
examples: **Yakushima is cleaned by volunteers.**
**Mt. Fuji is loved by Japanese people.**

exerciseSets.title: **Mt. Fuji will be enjoyed by people forever.**
exerciseSets.topic: 助じょ動どう詞しつきの　受うけ身み

grammarPoint.title: **Mt. Fuji will be enjoyed by people forever.**
grammarPoint.japaneseDescription: 助じょ動どう詞しつきの　受うけ身み：助じょ動どう詞しの　後うしろの　動どう詞しは　原げん形けいに　なる　ため、 助じょ動どう詞しつきの　受うけ身みの　形かたちは　〈助じょ動どう詞し＋ be ＋ 過か去こ分ぶん詞し〉と　なる。
grammarPoint.englishExplanation: When a modal verb precedes the passive structure, the modal is followed by the base form 'be', resulting in the structure 〈Modal + be + past participle〉. This allows expressing abilities, predictions, or obligations in the passive voice.
examples: **Mt. Fuji will be enjoyed by people forever.**
**Mt. Fuji can be seen in many ukiyo-e prints.**
